The table is the SCL-K-9 (Klaghofer & Brahler 2001), whose nine items are nine items of the SCL-90-R -- the paper states 'In order to have a more efficient screening instrument representing all nine scales of the original SCL-90-R, the SCL-K-9 was developed. The nine items singled out showed the greatest discriminant power to the average psychological distress level (GSI-90) ... From each scale, the item showing the highest correlation coefficient with the GSI-90 (see Table 1) was chosen.' So the wording is SCL-90-R wording, and the rights holder of the SCL-90-R is NCS Pearson, which sells it as a qualification-restricted commercial test (SCL-90-R store page, kits from $80.90, answer sheets 'include test items').
